statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band on a contained, twice-retraced overnight range, while Stress stays high on two-decade-high yields and a dense release schedule.
recommendation: Tail is below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON. A narrow danger window is flagged from 12:15 to 15:00 UTC covering ADP, the Core PCE and final GDP block, the US cash open and Chicago PMI. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: Contained overnight range keeps Tail low into the last Core PCE before the October FOMC
body: NQ futures trade near 30,664 after printing 30,737 and 30,540 overnight, a band of roughly 0.6% in which both extremes were retraced rather than held. ES is tighter still at 7,734 to 7,756, and VIX at 15.93 is easing near the low of its own range. Nasdaq-100 cash closed Monday's session at 30,339.33, up 0.21%, mid-range and about 90 points below the session high, so the most recent cash print also ended in a retracement rather than at an extreme. This is the second consecutive tight-range session and there is no observed directional efficiency, repeated extension or failed-retracement sequence, which is why Tail stays in the low band. The stress picture is different. The 10-year yield sits near 5.26% and the 30-year near 5.55 to 5.61%, the highest levels since 2007 and 2004 respectively, and yields have continued to rise even against a softer oil tape and dovish Fed commentary. That non-confirmation, September sector dispersion of roughly 10 percentage points between technology and financials, REITs or consumer discretionary, and visible megacap dispersion together justify a high Stress reading that can coexist with low Tail. The schedule is dense. ADP arrives at 12:15 and Core PCE, headline PCE and final Q2 GDP at 12:30, consensus near 0.3% MoM and 3.3 to 3.4% YoY on core. This is the last core PCE before the October 27-28 FOMC, where roughly 70% odds of a further hike are priced after September's move to 3.75-4.00%. The US cash open at 13:30 and Chicago PMI at 13:45 fall immediately behind it, and Micron reports fiscal Q4 after the 20:00 close on the final day of the quarter. Event importance and positioning are treated as Stress and Confidence inputs; conditional Tail is lifted only into the WATCH band across the release and opening-auction hours, and would require observed persistent one-way structure to move higher.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the past 24 hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment; the 14:00 UTC slot on September 29 has none and stays explicitly unavailable. The window opens in the WATCH band with Tail 20 to 24 and Stress in the mid to high 70s through the September 29 US session, peaking at Tail 24 at 15:00 UTC. From 20:00 UTC Tail crossed back under 20 and the mapped state returned to EA_ON, with Tail easing to 15 to 18 and Stress decaying steadily from 71 to 65 across the overnight session as the range tightened.
outlookSummary: The low Tail band is expected to hold through the European morning while NQ stays inside its overnight band. Conditional Tail lifts into the WATCH band for the 12:00 to 14:00 UTC hours covering ADP, the Core PCE and final GDP block, the US cash open and Chicago PMI, then decays through the US afternoon if the release is absorbed with normal retracements. A second conditional lift covers the quarter-end close and Micron's fiscal Q4 report and call from 19:00 to 21:00 UTC. The overnight path returns to a contained two-way baseline, with confidence declining purely as a function of forecast distance ahead of jobless claims and ISM Manufacturing on October 1 and payrolls on October 2.

forecast.analysis: Observed: NQ has printed both overnight extremes, 30,737 and 30,540, and trades near 30,664 inside that 0.6% band. Every probe retraced, so directional efficiency is absent and Tail stays in the low band. ES is similarly contained and VIX sits at 15.93.
drivers: Overnight NQ band 30,540-30,737; both extremes already retraced
ES band 7,734-7,756 is an unusually tight 0.3%
VIX 15.93, easing and near the low of its own range
Second consecutive tight range day ahead of US inflation data

forecast.analysis: European cash trade adds liquidity with no scheduled US catalyst in this hour. Absent a decisive break of the overnight band, the mean-reverting pattern of the past two sessions should persist. A sustained move outside 30,540-30,737 would be the first evidence against that.
drivers: European cash session liquidity, no scheduled US release
Overnight band 30,540-30,737 is the working invalidation level
Yields near two-decade highs remain the dominant macro pressure

forecast.analysis: European mid-morning. Pre-positioning into the 12:15 ADP and 12:30 PCE releases typically begins to thin two-way flow here. Conditional risk edges up only on the approach to those checkpoints, not on any structure observed so far.
drivers: Pre-release positioning into 12:15 ADP and 12:30 PCE begins
Order-book depth conditionally thins ahead of the release window
No observed one-way structure to extrapolate from

forecast.analysis: Final hour before the release block. Liquidity conditionally thins further and spreads widen as participants step back ahead of 12:15 and 12:30. Stress rises on that mechanical setup; Tail stays low because no persistent directional path has been observed.
drivers: Last hour before ADP 12:15 and Core PCE/GDP 12:30
Conditionally thinner book widens slippage without implying trend
Core PCE consensus +0.3% MoM, 3.3-3.4% YoY

Last core PCE before the Oct 27-28 FOMC decision

Chicago PMI 13:45 lands inside the opening auction
Watch whether the first pullback holds or fails
Yield-led repricing is the main continuation mechanism

forecast.analysis: First full cash hour, with EIA crude stocks at 14:30 against WTI near 89 dollars. Conditional risk eases if the open produces a normal retracement; it would persist only if price keeps extending after failed pullbacks. Treat the prior hour's structure as the test.
drivers: First full US cash hour after the release
EIA crude stocks 14:30 with WTI near 89 dollars
Failed retracement plus repeated extension would be the Tail trigger
Orderly two-way discovery would confirm decay instead

forecast.analysis: Post-open price discovery. If the release has been absorbed without persistent directional efficiency, conditional Tail returns to the low band and the mapped state reverts to EA_ON. Sector dispersion stays wide, which is a Stress input rather than a Tail input.
drivers: Release conditionally absorbed; two-way discovery resumes
September dispersion: XLK +4.4% against XLF, XLRE, XLY each -6%
Wide dispersion informs Stress and conviction, not Tail

forecast.analysis: Midday US session. Volume normally fades after the morning repricing and ranges compress. Conditional risk is the lowest of the cash session unless the morning has established structure that is still extending, which cannot be assumed from here.
drivers: Midday volume fade typically compresses the range
No post-release structure can be assumed at this distance
10-year near 5.26% remains the persistent background pressure

forecast.analysis: Early US afternoon lull with no scheduled catalyst. This is usually the most mean-reversion friendly part of the cash session. Quarter-end rebalancing flow builds later, so the conditional path here is compression rather than extension.
drivers: No scheduled catalyst in the early afternoon
Historically the most mean-reversion friendly cash hour
Quarter-end rebalancing flow builds into the close, not yet here

forecast.analysis: European cash has closed, removing cross-market hedging flow, and the US tape thins. Conditional risk stays low. The next genuine checkpoint is the quarter-end rebalancing window and the 20:00 cash close, not this hour.
drivers: European cash closed; cross-market hedging flow steps away
Thinner tape without a scheduled catalyst
Next checkpoint is quarter-end rebalancing into the close

forecast.analysis: Power hour on the final session of Q3, so market-on-close rebalancing imbalances can be larger than usual. This is a flow event rather than an information event: it can stretch price without establishing the failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail.
drivers: Quarter-end power hour; MOC imbalances larger than usual
Flow-driven stretch differs from an information-driven trend
Mapped policy state conditionally returns to WATCH on flow risk

forecast.analysis: Cash closes at 20:00 with the quarter-end MOC print, then Micron reports fiscal Q4 shortly after, with its call at 20:30. Guidance of about 50 billion dollars in revenue makes it a semiconductor bellwether landing in a thin post-close tape.
drivers: Quarter-end market-on-close print at 20:00
Micron fiscal Q4 results after the close; call 20:30
Guidance about 50bn revenue, 31 dollars adjusted EPS
Post-close liquidity is thin, so gaps are wider than ranges

forecast.analysis: Micron's call and its fiscal 2027 outlook are digested here. A large HBM or memory-pricing surprise can reprice semiconductors and drag index futures in a thin tape. Any resulting move is a gap-and-reprice risk, not evidence of a sustained no-retracement path.
drivers: Micron call underway; HBM4 and memory pricing in focus
Semiconductor repricing can transmit to index futures
Thin post-close book widens the move for a given flow
Gap risk is distinct from persistent one-way structure

forecast.analysis: Late US evening. The earnings reaction conditionally settles into a new range before Asian cash opens. Absent continued extension after the initial repricing, conditional Tail decays back toward the overnight baseline.
drivers: Earnings reaction conditionally settles into a fresh range
Asian cash has not yet opened; participation is minimal
Decay assumes the initial repricing found two-way interest

forecast.analysis: Asian cash opens and takes its cue from the US close and the Micron reaction. Overnight sessions in this regime have produced contained, mean-reverting ranges, so the conditional baseline is a normal two-way path rather than continuation.
drivers: Asian cash open re-prices the US close and Micron reaction
Recent overnight sessions have been contained and two-way

drivers: Asian session with no scheduled US catalyst
Range-bound conditional baseline consistent with recent overnights
Declining confidence reflects forecast distance only

forecast.analysis: Japanese and Korean cash trade dominate and semiconductor names there may still be carrying the Micron reaction. That is a sector conduit into index futures rather than a mechanism capable of producing persistent index-level one-way structure.
drivers: Japanese and Korean semis may still carry the Micron reaction
Sector conduit into futures, not an index-level trend mechanism
Contained conditional range remains the baseline

drivers: Quietest stretch of the Asian session
Recent overnight ranges have held inside the prior US cash range
Contained two-way movement is the conditional baseline

forecast.analysis: Mid to late Tokyo session with adequate liquidity and no scheduled US data. The low conditional Tail band assumes continued two-way behaviour, which the next hourly assessment will re-test against observed price rather than carry forward as fact.
drivers: Mid to late Tokyo session, adequate liquidity, no US data
Low conditional Tail assumes continued two-way behaviour

forecast.analysis: Final Tokyo hour before the 06:00 cash close. Asian closing flow can stretch index futures briefly, but in this regime the handover has more often marked the overnight turn than extended it, which supports holding the low conditional Tail band.
drivers: Final Tokyo hour ahead of the 06:00 cash close
Asian closing flow can stretch futures briefly

forecast.analysis: Tokyo has closed and European cash has not yet opened, the thinnest part of the 24-hour cycle. A move in this window carries less information about sustained structure than the same move in cash hours, so conditional Tail rises only marginally on liquidity.
drivers: Tokyo closed, European cash not yet open: thinnest liquidity
A move here says less about structure than one in cash hours

forecast.analysis: European cash opens and closes this forecast horizon. Conditional risk sits modestly above the overnight baseline on returning liquidity and positioning into that session's jobless claims and ISM Manufacturing, with payrolls on October 2 the week's main remaining checkpoint.
